title: Component Customization Contract v2
description: Contract declaring the freeze-line and the four config shapes a pre-rendered OCI component expects from the consumer (talos-platform-docs ADR-0024). Lives as customization.yaml next to the component's helm/ + manifests/ in the catalog repository. Note it is NOT inside the published OCI artifact: `task package` tars only kustomization.yaml + manifest.yaml, so a consumer reads this contract from the catalog repository at the tag they pin. Supersedes the ADR-0023 v1 contract.

freeze_line.description: The workload/config boundary (ADR-0024, calibrated-friction). The workload is the pre-rendered, signed, hardened baseline: the image digest is the hard consumer-admission anchor (cosign verifyImages); its other fields a consumer may overlay per-cluster without a catalog PR (a catalog PR changes the shared baseline for all consumers) — except platform-set fields like sync_wave that stay catalog-owned, and dangerous classes (hostPath, cluster-admin bindings) that the consumer-side ADR-0018 Kyverno safe-defaults discourage. config shapes (a-d) are the ergonomic consumer-input surface this contract models.

workload.description: Path to the pre-rendered, signed workload baseline (conventionally rendered/manifest.yaml); the image digest is hard-anchored at consumer admission, most other fields are consumer-overlayable per-cluster (platform-set fields like sync_wave stay catalog-owned) — ADR-0024.

provided_refs.description: Names under which the rendered workload expects config the consumer controls, by shape. Two ownership modes share these names: for a `required` shape the consumer AUTHORS the object; for an `optional` shape the artifact SHIPS the object with working content and the consumer replaces that content by kustomize patch. Empty {} for cluster-agnostic components.

env.description: Shape (a): ConfigMap consumed via envFrom (12-factor env scalars). Convention <component>-runtime-config.

config.description: Shape (b): ConfigMap/Secret mounted as a whole config file the app reads. Convention <component>-config.

secret.description: Shape (c): Secret consumed via envFrom or mounted. Convention <component>-runtime-secret.

provided_selectors.description: Shape (d): for each operator-assembled config kind, the label set the consumer CRs must carry; the rendered consuming CR declares the matching selector. Empty {} when the component has no operator-assembled config.

additionalProperties.description: Label set (key/value) the consumer CRs must carry to match the workload selector.

exposed_selectors.description: The INVERSE of provided_selectors: stable label sets a rendered workload object carries so a consumer's OWN object can select it (e.g. a Cilium LB-IPAM CiliumLoadBalancerIPPool serviceSelector pinning a LoadBalancer VIP without patching the signed Service). Declaring the label here makes it a versioned binding surface — a future rename is a contract change, not a silent break. Optional (additive to ADR-0024 v2): absent/{} when nothing external binds to this workload by label. Schema self-consistency only today; a render-time check that the workload actually carries each declared label is a follow-up (like config-mount #1 / selector #3). Schema-contract-parity for this new binding surface: (1) closed field set (additionalProperties:false); (2) duplicate keys are file corruption — YAML last-wins, surface not silently accept; (3) no version field — additions are backward-additive/optional, consumers detect change via the schema $id + JSON-Schema tooling, not a version marker; (4) this schema is a repo-SOT trusted-data file, so no untrusted-data sentinel applies; (5) declarative/mutable-in-place — a rename is a reviewed contract change.

additionalProperties.description: One exposed binding surface: the workload object kind and the stable label set a consumer selects on.

kind.description: Rendered workload object kind carrying the labels (e.g. Service).

labels.description: Stable label set the consumer's selecting object matches on. Consumer-supplied objects (the selecting pool/CR) are never in the signed artifact; only these labels are the contract.

required.description: What the consumer MUST supply, per shape — without it the workload does not function. Empty lists = nothing (cluster-agnostic). Keys that carry a working baked default and are supplied only to CHANGE behaviour belong under `optional`, never here; the two channels are disjoint.

env_keys.description: Shape (a): scalar keys the consumer must set in the env ConfigMap (provided_refs.env).

config_files.description: Shape (b): full config files the consumer authors; the workload mounts each at its path.

path.description: Absolute path of the FILE the workload reads — the volume mountPath plus the file name, e.g. /etc/booter/booter.yaml. It is a file path, never a bare mountPath: a ConfigMap volume projects every key as its own file. Identical semantics to optional.config_files[].path, deliberately: task validate:contract checks path uniqueness across the UNION of both channels, which is only meaningful while the two fields denote the same kind of value.

ref.description: ConfigMap/Secret name carrying the file (matches provided_refs.config or .secret). The pattern is the RFC 1123 DNS subdomain Kubernetes enforces for object names — dot-separated labels, no consecutive dots, no dot-adjacent hyphens — with its 253-character bound. Beyond charset hygiene it is load-bearing for the gate: an entry identity is built as <ref>|<key>, so a pipe character in either field would collide two distinct entries into a phantom duplicate. Both channels feed that identity, so both carry the pattern.

key.description: Key within the ref holding the file content. The pattern is the charset Kubernetes enforces for ConfigMap data keys, minus the two names it rejects outright (a single dot and a double dot); it also keeps the pipe character out of the identity string the gate builds.

secret_keys.description: Shape (c): keys the consumer must provide in the runtime secret (provided_refs.secret).

selector_crs.description: Shape (d): CRs the consumer must create and label so the operator assembles them.

kind.description: CR kind the consumer must create (e.g. ServiceMonitor, PrometheusRule).

label.description: Label set the CR must carry to match the rendered workload selector.

optional.description: What the consumer MAY supply to change behaviour, per shape — the counterpart to `required`. `required` = the consumer MUST set it or the workload does not function; `optional` = the artifact carries a working baked default and the component runs unset. This is the ADR-0024 calibrated-friction surface in its ergonomic form: a knob a consumer turns per-cluster without a catalog PR and without replacing the signed config. Additive and absent by default. Two of `required`'s four shapes are modelled: the env shape (DR-0004) and the config-file shape (DR-0005). A secret-key / selector channel is added when a component needs one (an unused shape would be unexercised semantics), and because this block is `additionalProperties: false` that addition is always an explicit, reviewed schema change. Six rules JSON Schema cannot express are enforced by `task validate:contract` over the real component files: an env name is not in both channels (S1) and is unique here (S2); a config-file (ref, key) identity is not in both channels (S3) and is unique within each channel (S4); a config-file `path` is unique across both channels together (S5); and an optional config-file `ref` is never the secret ref (S6), because `default` records baked content verbatim and this repository forbids real secrets. Two consequences a component author has to know: a consumer validating against a VENDORED copy of this schema predating the shape they use REJECTS the customization.yaml carrying it (closed root, `$id` deliberately unchanged — the validation error naming the unknown property is the only in-band signal); and renaming a shipped entry, removing it, or changing its `default` is BREAKING and SILENT (an env expansion falls back with no error; a renamed file ref leaves the consumer's kustomize patch on an object the workload no longer reads, and the patch may even keep applying cleanly while the old object lingers under Prune=false) — major bump plus migration note, never an in-place edit. Rationale and all five schema-contract-parity decisions in full: knowledge/decisions/DR-0004-optional-customization-keys.md (env shape) and knowledge/decisions/DR-0005-optional-config-file-channel.md (config-file shape).

env_keys.description: Shape (a): scalar keys the consumer MAY set in the env ConfigMap (provided_refs.env) to override a baked default. Each entry documents one placeholder that actually exists in the rendered config. Note the residual: no gate compares a declared key against the render, so a declared key with no matching placeholder is a knob that silently does nothing.

name.description: Env variable name exactly as it appears in the rendered config placeholder (e.g. INGESTER_REPLICATION_FACTOR for ${INGESTER_REPLICATION_FACTOR:1}). Unique within optional.env_keys and never also present in required.env_keys.

description.description: What the key does: the config path(s) it drives and the effect of changing it. Required — an undocumented knob is not a contract.

default.description: The value that applies when the consumer leaves the key unset, as a string, exactly as baked into the artifact. An empty string means the expanded value is empty — which may itself select an upstream default; say so in `description` when it does.

group.description: Optional grouping label for keys that only make sense set together (e.g. a cache's backend plus its addresses). DESCRIPTIVE ONLY: nothing validates that a consumer set every member of a group — it records the co-requirement for the reader.

config_files.description: Shape (b): whole config files the artifact BAKES with working content and the consumer MAY replace to change behaviour — the optional counterpart to required.config_files, which the consumer MUST author. Each entry documents one file the rendered workload already reads from a ConfigMap the artifact ships, so the component runs untouched. MECHANISM: the consumer does NOT write into the shipped object directly — it is part of the signed base and Argo reconciles it back. The consumer replaces the content per-cluster through `source.kustomize.patches` on that ConfigMap (ADR-0024 calibrated friction), exactly as for any other field of the base. ConfigMap only: a Secret is never a valid ref here, because `default` records the baked content verbatim and baking usable secret material into this repository violates AGENTS.md §Hard Constraints — `task validate:contract` refuses a ref equal to provided_refs.secret. Item fields mirror required.config_files (path/ref/key) plus optional.env_keys (description/default/group), because an optional file needs the same two facts an optional key does: what it drives, and what holds when the consumer supplies nothing. Residual: no gate compares a declared entry against the render, so a declared path/ref/key that no rendered volume actually mounts is a knob that silently does nothing.

path.description: Absolute path of the FILE the workload reads — the volume's mountPath plus the name the key projects to (e.g. /etc/customresourcestate/config.yaml for key config.yaml under mountPath /etc/customresourcestate), the convention required.config_files already uses. It is a file path, never a bare mountPath: a ConfigMap volume projects every key as its own file, so two replaceable keys of one ConfigMap carry two distinct paths here. Unique across required.config_files AND optional.config_files together — one path cannot hold two different files. Not representable: one (ref, key) mounted at two paths (e.g. into two containers); declare the one the consumer's replacement is about.

ref.description: Name of the ConfigMap carrying the file, matching provided_refs.config. Unlike required.config_files, this object IS shipped in the artifact with working content — the consumer replaces that content by kustomize patch, never by creating the object. Pin the name explicitly in the component's helm values where the chart would otherwise derive it from the release name: it is a consumer-facing contract value, so a chart-template change must not rename it silently. The pattern is the RFC 1123 DNS-subdomain charset Kubernetes enforces for object names, which also keeps `|` out of the (ref, key) identity string the gate builds.

key.description: Key within the ref holding the file content. The (ref, key) pair is this entry's identity: unique within optional.config_files and never also present in required.config_files. The pattern is the charset Kubernetes enforces for ConfigMap data keys, which also keeps `|` out of the identity string the gate builds.

description.description: What the file drives, the effect of replacing it, HOW a replacement takes effect (a projected ConfigMap file updates on the kubelet sync period, so state whether the workload re-reads it or the consumer must restart the pod), and any obligation that comes with it (e.g. RBAC the consumer must add for the resources the file names). Required — an undocumented knob is not a contract. Reload semantics live here rather than in a field of their own: the answer is per-workload prose, not a boolean.

default.description: The file content that applies when the consumer replaces nothing, as a string, VERBATIM as baked into the artifact — never a summary or a description of its effect. Verbatim is load-bearing: it is what lets a future render-vs-contract check compare this field against the rendered ConfigMap's data[key] and call a mismatch a defect. A component whose baked content is too large to inline usefully gets no prose escape hatch here; it needs a discriminated field of its own, added as an explicit reviewed schema change. An empty string means an empty file is baked — say so in `description`, together with what the workload does with it.

group.description: Optional grouping label for files that only make sense replaced together. DESCRIPTIVE ONLY: nothing validates that a consumer replaced every member of a group — it records the co-requirement for the reader.

sync_wave.description: ArgoCD sync-wave as a string (pre-rendered into the manifest; a platform property, not a cluster property — the consumer does not patch it).

external_dependencies.description: Other components (<sub-layer>/<component>) that must exist in the same cluster before this one runs sensibly.
